{{2016–17 American Athletic Conference men's basketball standings}}

The '''2016–17 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Cincinnati]] in the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team played its home games at [[Fifth Third Arena]], with a capacity of 13,176. The season marked the final year prior to major renovations to Fifth Third Arena.<ref>{{cite web|title=Fifth Third Arena|url=http://www.gobearcats.com/facilities/fifth-third-arena.html|website=GoBearcats.com|publisher=CBSi Advanced Media|access-date=25 May 2016}}</ref> The [[Cincinnati Bearcats|Bearcats]] were led by 11th-year head coach [[Mick Cronin (basketball)|Mick Cronin]] and were members of the [[American Athletic Conference]]. They finished the season 30–6, 16–2 to finish in second place in [[2016–17 American Athletic Conference men's basketball season|AAC play]]. They beat [[2016-17 Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball team|Tulsa]] and [[2016-17 UConn Huskies men's basketball team|UConn]] in the [[2017 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|AAC tournament]] before losing to [[2016-17 SMU Mustangs men's basketball team|SMU]] in the championship game. They received an at-large bid to the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 6 seed in the South region. They defeated No. 11-seeded [[2016-17 Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball team|Kansas State]] in the first round before losing to No. 3-seeded [[2016-17 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|UCLA]] in the second round.

==Previous season==
The [[2015–16 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team|Bearcats]] finished the [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2015–16 season]] with a record of 22–11, 12–6 in [[2015–16 American Athletic Conference men's basketball season|AAC play]] to finish in a tie for third place in conference. They lost to [[2015–16 UConn Huskies men's basketball team|UConn]] in four overtimes in the quarterfinals of the [[2016 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|AAC tournament]]. The Bearcats received an at-large bid as a No. 9 seed to the [[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they lost to [[2015–16 Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball team|Saint Joseph's]] in the first round.

==Preseason==
At AAC Media Day, Cincinnati was picked to win the AAC regular season title and senior guard [[Troy Caupain]] was voted as AAC Preseason Co-Player of the Year. In addition, [[Gary Clark (basketball)|Gary Clark]] and Caupain were named to the Preseason All-AAC First Team.<ref name="Preseason media">{{cite press release|title=Cincinnati Voted as 2016–17 American Men's Basketball Favorite|date=October 24, 2016|publisher=American Athletic|url=http://theamerican.org/news/2016/10/20/MBB_1020162600.aspx|access-date=October 24, 2016}}</ref>
